hero.text: Two papers of two hours, eighty marks each, weighted fifty-fifty. One tests reading, the other tests writing, and the second can be replaced by coursework.

blocks.title: Where these figures come from
text: Every figure on this page was read from Cambridge International's own syllabus documents: the [0500 syllabus for 2027, 2028 and 2029](https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/718783-2027-2029-syllabus.pdf) and the [0500 syllabus for 2024, 2025 and 2026](https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/635230-2024-2026-syllabus.pdf).

**The question-by-question detail comes from the 2027-2029 syllabus only.** Paper 1 was restructured for 2027 and Paper 2 Section A was divided into two parts, so a candidate sitting in 2026 should check the 2024-2026 syllabus for the paper they will actually be given. The component table, the durations, the weightings and the mark totals are the same in both.
Cambridge materials are linked, never copied. **RCF English is not affiliated with, endorsed by or approved by Cambridge Assessment International Education.**

blocks.title: This is not the same qualification as English as a Second Language
text: **First Language English (0500 and 0990)** is for students who use English as a first language. It assesses reading and writing only, and expects a first-language command of style.

**[English as a Second Language](global-english/igcse/english-as-a-second-language/) (0510, 0511, 0991, 0993)** assesses reading, writing, listening and speaking for learners using English alongside another first language.

They are separate syllabuses with separate papers, and **a school enters a candidate for one, not both** - Cambridge lists them among the syllabuses that cannot be combined in a single examination series. Revision material written for one will mislead you if you are sitting the other.

blocks.heading: The components
blocks.caption: All candidates take Paper 1, and then either Paper 2 or Component 3. The school decides which. Component 4 is optional and does not count towards the grade.
rows: Structured and extended writing questions on **three reading texts**. Externally assessed. Every candidate takes this.
An extended writing question and a composition task. Externally assessed.
Three extended writing assignments. Internally assessed, externally moderated.
Optional. Marks do **not** contribute to the overall grade; achievement is reported as grades 1 (high) to 5 (low) on the certificate.

blocks.title: The one decision that changes how you prepare
text: Paper 2 and Component 3 are worth the same and cover much the same writing skills, but they are not the same experience. **Paper 2 is two hours of examination writing** with a directed task and a composition chosen from four titles. **Component 3 is three assignments of 500 to 800 words each**, written over time and marked in your school.

This is a decision your **school** makes at entry, not one you make in the examination hall. Find out which one you are entered for before you spend a term revising for the wrong one - the composition practice transfers, but the timing practice does not.

blocks.heading: The assessment objectives
text: Ten objectives, five for reading and five for writing. They are worth learning by number, because the syllabus attaches them to individual questions and they tell you exactly what each question is buying.

parts.heading: Reading
bullets: **R1** demonstrate understanding of explicit meanings
**R2** demonstrate understanding of implicit meanings and attitudes
**R3** analyse, evaluate and develop facts, ideas and opinions, using appropriate support from the text
**R4** demonstrate understanding of how writers achieve effects and influence readers
**R5** select and use information for specific purposes

parts.heading: Writing
bullets: **W1** articulate experience and express what is thought, felt and imagined
**W2** organise and structure facts, ideas and opinions for deliberate effect
**W3** use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures appropriate to context
**W4** use language appropriate to purpose and to engage the audience
**W5** make accurate use of spelling, punctuation and grammar

parts.heading: What the numbering is actually for
text: R1 and R2 are the difference between what a text says and what it means, and almost every reading question tests both. R4 - how writers achieve effects - is the one students most often leave out, and on Paper 1 it carries part of two separate questions.

On the writing side, **W5 is spelling, punctuation and grammar, and it is one of five objectives on every writing task.** It is the easiest of the ten to lose and the only one you can protect by leaving five minutes at the end.

items.title: Paper 1: Reading
text: Four questions of twenty marks each, on three texts. Comprehension, summary, a language task and an extended response.
bullets: 2 hours, 80 marks, 50%
Three reading texts: A, B and C
Two of the four questions include writing marks

items.title: Paper 2: Directed Writing and Composition
text: A directed writing task built on one or two short texts, and a composition chosen from four titles.
bullets: 2 hours, 80 marks, 50%
Section A 40 marks, Section B 40 marks
Two descriptive and two narrative titles

blocks.heading: Component 3: the Coursework Portfolio
text: The alternative to Paper 2, worth the same 80 marks and the same 50%. Candidates submit **three assignments of about 500 to 800 words each**, which may be completed in any order.
bullets: **Assignment 1 (30 marks):** writing to discuss, argue and/or persuade, in response to a text or texts.
**Assignment 2 (25 marks):** writing to describe.
**Assignment 3 (25 marks):** writing to narrate.
It is **internally assessed and externally moderated**, which means your teacher marks it and Cambridge checks the marking.
Assignment 1 is the only one of the three that carries reading marks, because it responds to a text. The other two are assessed on writing alone.

blocks.title: Component 4 counts, but not towards your grade
text: The Speaking and Listening Test lasts about 10 to 12 minutes and is optional. Its marks do **not** contribute to the grade you receive for the written components.

Instead, where a candidate performs to an appropriate standard, the certificate records achievement as **grades 1 (high) to 5 (low)**, separately endorsed alongside the main grade. It is worth doing and it is not worth revising at the expense of Paper 1.

blocks.heading: What changes for 2027
text: The first examinations on the new syllabus are in 2027. **The shape of the qualification does not change:** the same two papers, the same two hours each, the same 80 marks each, the same 50/50 weighting, the same coursework alternative and the same optional speaking test.
What changes is inside the papers.

parts.heading: Paper 1
bullets: The total mark is unchanged and the duration is unchanged.
**The paper has been restructured** so that candidates can navigate it more efficiently and use their time better.
The questions are still based on three reading texts.

parts.heading: Paper 2
bullets: The total mark is unchanged and the duration is unchanged.
**Section A: the reading texts are shorter** - the total word count has been reduced to 550 to 650 words.
**The directed writing task has been divided into two parts,** 1(a) and 1(b), to help candidates with their comprehension of the text or texts.
**Question 1(a) assesses R3 and R4**, and R4 was not previously assessed in this paper.
Question 1(b) carries 10 marks for reading and 25 for writing.
**Section B is unchanged** in what it asks for.
The marking criteria have been updated across both sections.

parts.heading: Components 3 and 4
bullets: **Component 3:** the forms in which candidates write have been updated and clarified. There are **no changes to the mark allocations**. The marking criteria have been updated.
**Component 4:** no changes to the tasks or mark allocations. The marking criteria have been updated.

blocks.title: If you are sitting in November 2026
text: You are on the **2024-2026 syllabus**, not the one described question by question on the paper pages here. The components, the timings, the marks and the weightings are identical, so everything on this page applies to you.

What may not apply is the internal structure of Paper 1 and the two-part directed writing task on Paper 2. Check the [2024-2026 syllabus](https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/635230-2024-2026-syllabus.pdf) and practise on past papers from your own series rather than on specimen material for 2027.

blocks.heading: 0500 and 0990: which code is yours
text: Cambridge publishes First Language English under two codes. The syllabus content is the same; the grading scale is not.

**0500** is graded **A* to G**, which the syllabus states directly. **0990** is the version graded **9 to 1**. Which one a school enters candidates for depends on the scale it wants on the certificate rather than on any difference in what is taught.

**Check your entry code on your statement of entry.** If it is 0990, use the 0990 syllabus page on the Cambridge site for the grading information, since this page was built from the 0500 syllabus documents.

hero.text: Three texts, four questions, twenty marks each. Two hours. Every candidate takes this paper.

blocks.title: Which syllabus this page describes
text: The question structure below is from the **0500 syllabus for 2027, 2028 and 2029**. Paper 1 was restructured for 2027, so if you are sitting in 2026 the paper you are given may be arranged differently. The duration, the total mark and the three texts are the same in both syllabuses.

Read from Cambridge's [0500 syllabus for 2027-2029](https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/718783-2027-2029-syllabus.pdf). Cambridge materials are linked, never copied; the methods on this page are RCF English's own. RCF English is not affiliated with, endorsed by or approved by Cambridge Assessment International Education.

blocks.title: Two things worth noticing about that table
text: **Sixty of the eighty marks are reading marks**, but twenty are writing marks, on Q2(a) and Q4. This is a reading paper that still asks you to write well in two places, and candidates who treat it as pure comprehension give those twenty marks away.
**Text C carries forty marks** - both Q3 and Q4 are set on it. It is worth reading Text C most carefully of the three, and worth reading Q3 and Q4 together before you answer either.

blocks.heading: Question 1: Comprehension (20 marks)
text: On **Text A**. A series of sub-questions, including short answers testing understanding of **both explicit and implicit meanings** - R1 and R2. All twenty marks are reading marks.
bullets: **Answer the number of points the marks ask for.** A two-mark sub-question wants two things; a third earns nothing and costs time you will want for Question 4.

**Explicit and implicit are different jobs.** Some sub-questions want what the text states; others want what it implies about a person's attitude or feeling. Read the question stem for which is being asked.
**Use your own words where the question asks for them,** and quote where it does not. Copying a whole sentence to answer an inference question rarely scores.
**Stay inside any line references given.** They are a boundary, not a suggestion.
**Time:** about 25 minutes.

blocks.heading: Question 2: Summary task (20 marks)
text: On **Text B**, in two parts.

**2(a)** is a selective summary **in your own words**, written as continuous writing of **no more than 120 words**. It carries **10 reading marks** (R1, R2 and R5 - selecting and using information for a specific purpose) and **5 writing marks** (W1, W2 and W3).
**2(b)** is a short-answer question testing understanding of **attitudes and opinions**, worth **5 reading marks**.

parts.heading: How 2(a) is actually won and lost
bullets: **The word limit is a limit, not a target.** No more than 120 words. Going over risks the writing marks and wastes minutes.
**Continuous writing means prose,** not bullet points and not a list. Five of the fifteen marks are for how it is written.
**Own words is the instruction that carries the marks.** Lifting phrases from Text B loses reading marks even when the content selected is right.
**Select, do not survey.** R5 is *select and use information for specific purposes*. Find the points that answer the question asked and leave out everything else, however interesting.
**Count the points first, then write.** Most candidates who run over 120 words did not plan which points were going in.
**Time:** about 20 minutes for 2(a) and 5 for 2(b).

blocks.heading: Question 3: Short-answer questions and language task (20 marks)
text: On **Text C**, in two halves, each worth 10 marks and both of them reading marks.
**The short-answer questions** are a series of sub-questions requiring answers of different lengths, testing R1, R2 and **R4 - how writers achieve effects and influence readers**.
**The language task** asks you to write **about 200 to 250 words** on Text C, testing the same three objectives.

parts.heading: The language task is where R4 lives
bullets: **Choose fewer words and say more about each.** A language answer that quotes fifteen phrases and comments on none of them scores below one that takes six and explains what each does to a reader.

**Name the effect, not the device.** *This is a metaphor* earns nothing. *This metaphor makes the crowd sound like weather - something that happens to you rather than something people are doing* earns the mark.
**Take the second step.** Say what the choice implies, or what it stops the reader from thinking. That step is the difference between explaining and analysing.
**Watch the length.** 200 to 250 words is short. It is about four tight paragraphs or three generous ones.
**Time:** about 10 minutes for the short answers, 20 for the language task.

blocks.heading: Question 4: Extended response to reading (20 marks)
text: Also on **Text C**. You write **about 250 to 300 words**, responding in **one of the following text types: letter, report, journal, speech, interview or article**.

It carries **10 reading marks** (R1, R2, R3 and R5) and **10 writing marks** (W1, W2 and the rest of the writing objectives). It is the only question on the paper that splits its marks evenly between reading and writing.
bullets: **The form is stated and it is assessed.** A speech and a report do not sound the same. Open in the register you have been given, in the first sentence, not the third.

**R3 is the objective that lifts this answer:** *analyse, evaluate and develop facts, ideas and opinions, using appropriate support from the text.* **Develop** is the word to notice. You are expected to go beyond the text, not merely to repeat it in a new form.
**Everything you invent must be anchored in Text C.** Free invention loses reading marks; inference the text supports gains them.
**Ten writing marks is a fifth of the paper's reading half.** Paragraph it, vary the sentences, and spell carefully.
**Time:** about 30 minutes, and do not let Questions 1 to 3 eat it.

blocks.title: A timing plan for Paper 1
text: **0-10 min** read all three texts once, and all four questions.
**10-35 min** Question 1, comprehension.
**35-60 min** Question 2, summary and the short answer.
**60-90 min** Question 3, short answers and language task.
**90-115 min** Question 4, extended response.
**115-120 min** check spelling, punctuation and paragraphing in Q2(a) and Q4 - the two places on this paper where writing is marked.

hero.text: Two sections of forty marks. One builds on a text you are given; the other is yours from a title. Two hours.

blocks.title: Which syllabus this page describes
text: The structure below is from the **0500 syllabus for 2027, 2028 and 2029**. Section A was divided into two parts for 2027 and the reading texts were shortened, so a candidate sitting in 2026 will meet a differently arranged Section A. The duration, the total mark and the two-section shape are the same in both syllabuses.

Read from Cambridge's [0500 syllabus for 2027-2029](https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/718783-2027-2029-syllabus.pdf). Cambridge materials are linked, never copied. RCF English is not affiliated with, endorsed by or approved by Cambridge Assessment International Education.

blocks.heading: Where the 80 marks sit
rows: Question 1(a), a structured question on the text(s)
Question 1(b), the directed writing task, about 250-350 words
One from four titles, about 350-450 words

blocks.title: Sixty-five of these eighty marks are writing marks
text: Paper 1 is mostly a reading paper. This one is not: **65 of its 80 marks are for writing**, and W5 - spelling, punctuation and grammar - is one of the five writing objectives on every single one of them.
That makes the last five minutes of each hour the highest-value five minutes on the paper. Nothing else you can do in five minutes is worth as much.

blocks.heading: Section A: Directed Writing (40 marks)
text: One question in two parts, based on **one or two texts totalling 550 to 650 words**.

parts.heading: Question 1(a): 5 marks
text: A structured question that lets you analyse, evaluate and demonstrate your understanding of the text or texts. It tests **R3** (analyse, evaluate and develop facts, ideas and opinions, using appropriate support) and **R4** (how writers achieve effects and influence readers).
bullets: **This part is new for 2027,** and R4 was not previously assessed on this paper at all.
It is five marks. Answer it properly and briefly - about five minutes - and do not let it become an essay.
Treat it as the reading you need anyway. The understanding it asks for is the understanding 1(b) is built on, so it is a free warm-up rather than an extra task.

parts.heading: Question 1(b): 35 marks
text: You **use, develop and evaluate** the information in the text or texts to write a **discursive, argumentative or persuasive speech, letter, article or report** of about **250 to 350 words**.
It carries **10 reading marks** (R1, R2, R3, R5) and **25 writing marks** (W1 to W5).
bullets: **Twenty-five of the thirty-five marks are for the writing itself.** The reading is the raw material; the marks are mostly for what you build with it.
**Develop and evaluate, do not summarise.** Repeating the text in a new form answers only the reading half and answers it thinly. Take a position and argue it.
**The form is named, and it is assessed.** A speech to an audience, a letter to a person, an article for readers and a report for a body all sound different. Signal the form in your first sentence.
**Use both texts if two are given.** Ignoring one is the quickest way to lose reading marks here.
**250 to 350 words is tight.** Two or three developed points beat five thin ones, and a concession you then answer is worth more than another point.
**Time:** about 55 minutes for the whole of Section A, including planning.

blocks.heading: Section B: Composition (40 marks)
text: One question from a choice of **four titles: two descriptive and two narrative**. You use the title to develop and write a composition of about **350 to 450 words**.
All forty marks are writing marks, across all five writing objectives - W1 to W5. There is no reading to do and nowhere to hide.

parts.heading: Choosing between descriptive and narrative
bullets: **Descriptive writing has no plot to rescue it.** It is marked on the precision of the seeing and the control of the language, and it fails when it becomes a list of adjectives.
**Narrative writing has a plot to go wrong.** In 350 to 450 words there is no room for a beginning, a middle, an end and a twist. One incident, told well, beats a whole story told at speed.
**Choose on which title gives you specific material,** not on which type you prefer in the abstract. A vague title in your favourite mode is worse than a concrete title in the other one.
**Decide in the first two minutes and do not change your mind at minute fifteen.**

parts.heading: What the forty marks reward
bullets: **W1 - articulate experience.** Something has to be genuinely observed, even if it is invented. Precision is what makes invention convincing.

**W2 - organise and structure for deliberate effect.** The order of your paragraphs should be a decision. A description that moves from far to near, or a narrative that opens after the event and looks back, is structured; one that simply proceeds is not.
**W3 - a range of vocabulary and sentence structures.** Range means variety used for effect, not long words used for their own sake. A short sentence after three long ones is range.
**W4 - language appropriate to purpose and to engage the audience.** The register has to hold from the first line to the last.
**W5 - spelling, punctuation and grammar.** A fifth of the objectives on a forty-mark task.
**Time:** about 55 minutes, including five planning and five checking.

blocks.title: A timing plan for Paper 2
text: **0-10 min** read the Section A text(s) and both parts of Question 1; read the four Section B titles and choose.
**10-15 min** Question 1(a).
**15-25 min** plan 1(b): your position, your three points, your form.
**25-55 min** write 1(b).
**55-60 min** check 1(b) for sentence endings and spelling.
**60-70 min** plan the composition.
**70-110 min** write it.
**110-120 min** check it. This is the single most valuable ten minutes on the paper, because every mark in this section is a writing mark.

rows: Qualification page: syllabus, specimen materials and resources

blocks.title: Why there is no list of past papers here
text: Cambridge distributes most past papers and mark schemes to **registered schools** through the School Support Hub, not to the public. A site that publishes a shelf of 0500 past papers is either linking to material it is not entitled to share or hosting copies of it.

**Ask your teacher or your school's examinations officer.** They have access to the Support Hub, and the papers they can give you are the right series for your entry, which matters more than quantity.

The **specimen papers** are published openly, and for the 2027 syllabus they are the most useful single document available to a candidate, because the paper has been restructured and past papers from earlier series will not show you the new arrangement.

blocks.title: Read the syllabus itself - it is short and it is specific
text: Almost no student reads the syllabus, and for 0500 it is a mistake. It states, for every question on both papers, exactly which assessment objectives are being tested and how many marks each is worth.

That is not background information. Knowing that Question 2(a) carries five writing marks, or that Question 1(a) on Paper 2 tests R4, tells you how to spend your minutes. It takes twenty minutes to read the assessment sections and it is the highest-value twenty minutes of preparation available.

blocks.title: Original RCF model paper
text: There is not yet an RCF model paper for 0500. The four GCSE English Language boards each have one - see the [AQA](global-english/gcse/aqa/papers/rcf-model-paper-2/), [Edexcel](global-english/gcse/edexcel/papers/), [OCR](global-english/gcse/ocr/papers/rcf-model-component-1/) and [Eduqas](global-english/gcse/eduqas/papers/rcf-model-component-2/) model papers - and a 0500 pair will follow the same pattern: original texts, verified structure, a separate marking guide and clear labelling as unofficial practice material.

In the meantime, the [Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language model paper](global-english/igcse/english-as-a-second-language/papers/) is useful for the reading-comprehension habits, though its questions are set at a different level and its mark allocations are not the same.
